reviews.title: Misleading and Extremely Frustrating
reviews.text:
I am incredibly disappointed with Everand and the way the subscription upgrade was presented. I upgraded to the $16.99/month Premium plan because I was under the impression that paying more would give me greater access to books. Instead, after upgrading, I discovered that many of the books I had already saved—including titles I saved years ago when the service was still called Scribd—were suddenly locked.

What makes this even more frustrating is that I am currently writing a paper and one of the books I am required to read is now unavailable to me until the middle of next month. I am paying MORE for the supposedly “better” Premium subscription, yet somehow I have less access to the books I actually need.

Everand needs to be much more upfront about what happens when customers change subscription plans. If upgrading means previously available or saved books can become locked behind monthly unlocks, that needs to be clearly disclosed BEFORE someone pays more money. Customers should not have to discover these restrictions after upgrading.

For anyone considering switching to the $16.99/month plan because you think it will automatically give you better or broader access to your saved books, please make sure you understand exactly what you are paying for first. I certainly wish that had been made clearer to me.

This experience feels incredibly misleading and has been a complete waste of money for me. I expected more access after upgrading—not to be locked out of books I was alre

reviews.title: No Longer Worth the Subscription
reviews.text:
I was an Everand subscriber for years because it offered something unique: a true subscription that encouraged discovery. I could browse, sample new authors, and read or listen without constantly calculating whether a book was “worth” spending a credit on.

The new unlock model completely changes that experience. At this point, Everand is essentially an Audible-style credit system, except you don’t actually own the books you unlock. If I can only access one or a few premium books each month, I’d rather buy them through Audible, where they remain in my library permanently.

I understand that licensing costs have changed, but this new model no longer offers enough value to justify the subscription. The service has lost what made it stand out from its competitors.

I’ll be cancelling my subscription and putting that money toward library memberships that include Hoopla and Libby instead. Those services provide a much better value for readers and listeners like me.

I truly hope Everand reconsiders its direction, because it used to be one of my favorite subscriptions.

reviews.title: Disgusted Customer
reviews.text:
This app has one of the most anti-consumer policies I’ve come across.

I genuinely enjoyed using it and spent my own money unlocking multiple books. Then life got busy, and I didn’t have time to listen. Instead of continuing to pay for a subscription I wasn’t using, I paused the subscription assuming I could still access the books I’d already purchased.

Apparently not.

Requiring an active subscription just to listen to books you have already paid to unlock is absurd. Once I’ve paid for content, it should not be held hostage behind another monthly fee. This app has sadly not been so customer-friendly. It’s simply a cash grab.

Policies like this punish loyal customers who have already invested money in your platform. If you’re considering this app, be aware that “unlocking” a book doesn’t really mean you own access to it unless you keep paying. That is disappointing, misleading, and enough for me to take my business elsewhere.

reviews.title: Constantly starts my book over. So frustrating!

reviews.title: Absolutely gutted
reviews.text: I loved this app, but instantly regretted the switch to the new subscriptions. Lost my legacy subscription and with this one your access is severely limited. There is literally no point now it’s completely lost its USP and sold out its long term subscribers. I would of been happy to pay a higher subscription price to retain access to the library but this new version is the absolute worst

reviews.title: New subscription sucks!
reviews.text: Like most reviews mentioned already, since the new subscription model kicked off, it’s gone completely down hill. Leaving the app unfortunately like everybody else for the same reason. Company got greedy and still seem to ignore what the people, their customers are complaining about. Bad new subscription model no longer worth the money. CANCELING my subscription and going elsewhere!

reviews.title: Used to be good but they have ruined it
reviews.text: Have just unsubscribed having used it for many years. This used to be a great app but they have ruined it. It is no longer clear which books are available or why. Just show me the books I can download or give a very clear indication as to how I can download them (pay or whatever) but at the moment you just get a book with the download bit greyed out with no explanation as to why or what you need to do to access it. Just irritating. Switching to a credit system leaves it indistinguishable from other, better, apps.

reviews.title: Amazing before the update
reviews.text: Before you could read so many books whenever and now they’ve updated it to a credit system, limiting what you can read and the how many. Boooo it was so so good before.

reviews.title: Downgrade to increase profit
reviews.text: I used to get immense vale from Scribd the Everand. The range of books available for a single price was immense. A library in my pocket, on my tablet and PC. Then over a year ago it changed. Now no longer unlimited but credit base. 2 subscribers options for 1 or 3 credits. The books are only on loan, so I am overpaying for a service where I am restricted. I used the service for research. No I’ve cancelled. Buy direct from Kindle or elsewhere, they are no longer good value.

reviews.title: Fed up waiting
reviews.text: After using my free trial credit I lived the app so much that I wanted to subscribe to plus and get the 3 credits but it makes you wait till the end of the trial so I have to wait a week now to actually use the app again??? What’s the point? I ended up going with another app instead of waiting. This is such a dumb design.

reviews.title: poor availability
reviews.text: I understand that content access is not unlimited and that sometimes i have to wait. but to suddenly lock the book i am in the middle of reading until the end of the month is ridiculous.

reviews.title: Formerly leading app falls victim to tech greed
reviews.text: I'm a long time subscriber and I'm now actively looking for alternatives. Instead of delivering much needed interface improvements, this app which I've been subscribed to since before it's rebrand from Scribd, was a forever app for me because you pay one subscription fee a month and have access to the entire catalogue. The model has now changed to a credits system which makes it pretty much distinguishable from audible and all the other audiobook and ebook apps. They have been destroyed what was the core USP of using this app and offered very little in return. I'm not exaggerating when I say I was evangelical to others about recommending this app.  I'm now actually looking for alternatives. Well done to whoever was in charge of this decision to change the subscription for signing the app's death sentence. I've heard from customer service the reasoning behind the change and it is illogical by any measure.
